outlet.name: ABC News (US)
outlet.summary: ABC News is leading with the collapse of US-Canada trade talks and the 50% tariffs that took effect overnight, alongside Trump administration moves on water, personnel and a run of overseas violence and piracy stories.

items.headline: US slaps 50% duties on Canadian goods as trade negotiations collapse
items.detail: The tariffs on roughly $28 billion of Canadian products, from hockey sticks to wine and dairy, took effect at 12:01 a.m. ET Saturday after Prime Minister Mark Carney suspended talks over what he called unfair last-minute changes to the US terms, and he pledged Canada would retaliate dollar for dollar.

items.headline: Interior Department imposes sharp Colorado River water reductions on three states
items.detail: With Lake Powell and Lake Mead at critical levels and the basin states unable to agree among themselves, the US Department of the Interior stepped in on Friday and ordered steep cuts to Colorado River deliveries for Arizona, California and Nevada.

items.headline: Justice Department pardon attorney Ed Martin exits his post
items.detail: Trump announced Friday that Martin, a former US attorney for the District of Columbia, is leaving the department to work on legal fights around the upcoming midterm election and the 2028 presidential race.

items.headline: Swedish police identify teenage girl as the person killed in school sword attack
items.detail: An 18-year-old man armed with a sword attacked the Brinell School in Fagersta, northwest of Stockholm, during class on Friday, killing a 17-year-old girl and wounding three others, two of them severely.

items.headline: Armed Somali hijackers seize oil tanker in waters off Yemen
items.detail: Six armed pirates boarded the Eritrean-flagged tanker M.T. Sibu 1 on Thursday about 136 nautical miles east of al-Mukalla, Yemen, and steered it toward Somalia's Puntland coast in what officials describe as part of a broader resurgence of piracy in the region.
